Subject: Baba Yaga's hut on chicken legs.
Style: Slavic folk art.

spec.name: Baba Yaga's Hut on Chicken Legs
spec.description: A Slavic folk-art diorama: a carved log izba with a red-trimmed gable roof, standing on two giant scaly chicken legs inside a skull-post fence on a small forest clearing.
spec.layout: Everything is centred on x = 0 and faces +Z, which is the front door and stairs. A round clearing disc (radius 3.5, top y 0.2) is the only floor piece. The izba floats on two chicken legs standing at x = ±0.75, z about 0.1, with feet planted at y 0.2 and toes splayed forward. Bottom to top: clearing y 0 to 0.2; legs y 0.2 to 2.0; a hut floor platform from y 1.85 to 2.0 (footprint x ±1.4, z ±1.3); honey-brown log walls y 2.0 to 3.5 (outer faces x ±1.3, z ±1.2, with log ends and rings sticking out 0.1 at the corners); then a steep gable roof with eaves at y 3.4 and x ±1.85, ridge at y 4.9 running along z from -1.65 to 1.75, overhanging the front. The front gable (door side, +Z) holds the door and the porch: a landing at z 1.2 to 2.0 and steep stairs down to the clearing, ending at z 3.1. A stubby brick chimney sits on the left rear slope. A horse-head ridge finial (konyok) crowns the front and back ends of the ridge. Folk art shows through one repeated motif, the six-petal rosette and sun, in red, yellow, blue and white. It appears on the door, window platbands, gable sunburst, porch balusters, fence posts and the clearing's border band. Carved platbands with zigzag cut-outs frame every window. Fretted barge-boards (polotentse) hang from the gable edges. Shingles alternate two browns with scalloped ends. The legs are chunky and bright yellow, with thick feathery rust-and-cream trousers at the top, scaled shanks, a spur, and three big dark claws plus a back toe on each foot. A skull-on-stake fence rings the clearing, with an open gap at the front for the stairs and a pair of gate posts. Birch trunks stand at the back corners, red-and-white fly-agaric mushrooms, flowers and stones decorate the edge, and a mortar and pestle rests near the stairs. The whole look is a chunky, simple primitive base with painted ornament built from small separate parts, and every surface is one flat colour.

parts.builds: Both giant chicken legs, mirrored, each running hip, knee (forward), hock (back) and ankle with a continuous smooth-skinned scaly tube. The tarsus is yellow (scaleYellow) with scaleDark scale plates, bands or ridges as small seated parts, and a sharp spur on the back of the hock. The thigh and knee wear a big shaggy trouser of overlapping feather blades in a root-to-tip palette (featherRust at the root, folkWhite and folkBlack tips), starting at y 2.0 so it tucks under the hut platform at hutUnderside around the hip mounts. The foot has three forward toes (toeL1 centre, toeL2 inner, toeL3 outer; toeR1 to toeR3 mirrored) and a back toe (toe4), each a tapered tube with knuckle bumps and a big curved dark claw (folkBlack, with a folkWhite highlight). Toe bottoms rest just in the clearing (ankle y 0.3, toe radius about 0.09). Ankle gets a folk-art red band with tiny yellow dots. Rigs: sweeps skinned over the leg chains, toes on digit joints. Shares the same left and right leg design, mirrored by sign of x.
parts.attaches: Hips at mounts hipL and hipR tuck under hutUnderside (y 1.85); feet plant at ankleL and ankleR just into groundTop (y 0.2). The feathers hide the seam at the hut platform.

parts.builds: The izba body. Floor platform (y 1.85 to 2.0, x ±1.4, z ±1.3) of dark planks with underside crossbeams and root-like knobs. Log walls y 2.0 to 3.5 built from stacked horizontal cylinders (about 6 courses, alternating logMid, logDark and logLight), outer faces at x ±1.3 and z ±1.2. Log ends protrude 0.1 at the four corners (notched corner crossings) and each end carries a small logEnd disc with a dark ring. A top plate logDark at y 3.5 and a moss patch or two (moss) on the base logs. Front wall: a door at doorCenter (x ±0.4, y 2.0 to 3.1) hung on the doorHinge joint, painted folkBlue with a folkRed border frame, yellow six-petal rosettes and a sun in the centre, iron-black hinge straps and a ring handle (folkBlack). It sits slightly proud of the wall. Left and right side windows at windowLeft and windowRight, and a back window at windowBack (opening about 0.5 wide by 0.6 tall, glowing warm folkYellow or glowWarm panes with folkBlack cross muntins). Each has carved platbands around it (folkRed frame, folkWhite zigzag cut-outs, a little folkBlue crown with a rosette on top, an apron below) and an open pair of shutters flat against the wall painted folkBlue with folkYellow rosette dots. The corner posts carry a thin folkRed painted stripe.
parts.attaches: Sits on hutFloor (y 2.0) over the legs at hutUnderside. Wall top at wallTop (y 3.5) meets the roof part. The front face at z 1.2 meets the porch landing at porchLanding and the stairs. Door rides doorHinge; everything else rides hut.

parts.builds: The steep folk gable roof and everything above wallTop. Two roof planes (thick slabs or lofts) run from eaveLeft or eaveRight (x ±1.85, y 3.4) up to the ridge at y 4.9, z -1.65 to 1.75, with a front overhang. They are covered by rows of scalloped shingle plates alternating shingleDark and shingleLight, and moss (moss) along the lower edges. A ridge beam (logDark) carries a carved horse-head finial (konyok) at ridgeFront and ridgeBack, painted folkRed with folkYellow trim and folkBlack eyes. A front gable triangle filled with vertical planks (logLight and logMid) fills from wallTop (y 3.5, x ±1.35) up to a point at about y 4.85. A round attic window sits at its centre with a folkYellow sunburst of 8 rays and a folkBlue ring, and a rosette row beneath. The gable edges wear fretted barge-boards (polotentse) in folkRed with folkWhite zigzag cut-outs and hanging pendant ends at the eaves. On the left rear slope a brick chimney (stoneDark with stone caps, folkRed brick courses) rises from chimneyBase, topped by a few puffs of smoke clumps (smoke) up to y 5.5. Small bone-white skull or rosette decorations are optional on the ridge.
parts.attaches: Roof eaves rest at wallTop (y 3.5) on the wall top plate; the gable triangle sits on the front wall at frontGable. The chimney stands on chimneyBase. Rides the hut joint.

parts.builds: The front porch and steep stair. A landing platform (planks logMid, edge beam logDark) with top at y 2.0, x ±0.85, z 1.2 to 2.0, at porchLanding. Eight steps run from stairTop (0, 2.0, 2.0) down to stairBottom (0, 0.2, 3.1), each a plank with rise about 0.225 and run 0.14, two stringers (logDark), and the front edge of each step carries a thin folkRed stripe with yellow dot accents. Railings on both sides: turned balusters (folkWhite with folkRed rings, small rosette caps) and a sloped handrail (logLight) following the stair, with carved newel posts topped with folkYellow balls at the landing. A hanging lantern (folkBlack frame, glowing glowWarm pane) on a bracket by the door at the landing's front-left. Small props on the landing and steps: a twig broom leaning on the rail (logLight handle, featherRust straw), a wooden bucket (logMid with folkBlack hoops), and strings of dried mushrooms or herb bundles (folkRed, folkWhite, folkGreen) hanging from a short beam at the landing's left edge.
parts.attaches: Landing meets the front wall at z about 1.2 near hutFloor and porchLanding. Stairs end at stairBottom on groundTop. Rides hut, whose stairs bottom just touches the clearing.

parts.builds: The diorama base and its dressing, kept simpler than the hut. A low round clearing disc (radius 3.5, y 0 to 0.2) in earth, with a grass cap (grass, with grassDark tufts as small cones, broad folk-style blades) and a dirt path (earth) from the gate to stairBottom. A folk border band around the rim: alternating folkRed and folkWhite wedges and folkBlue dots, repeating the rosette motif every ~0.7 m. A skull fence: stakes (logDark, pointed tops, one every ~0.45 m at radius about 3.15 with a gap of about ±22° around +Z) each topped with a folkWhite skull whose eye sockets glow glowGreen. Every third stake wears a folkRed painted band with a yellow dot. Two thicker gate posts at gatePostL and gatePostR carry bigger skulls. Behind the hut: two birch trunks (folkWhite with folkBlack bark dashes) at about (±2.7, z -2.3) rising to y 4.3, with a few angled branches and small folkGreen leaf plates. Along the fence and the sides, clusters of fly-agaric mushrooms (folkRed caps with folkWhite spots, folkWhite stems), big six-petal folk flowers (folkYellow, folkRed and folkBlue petals with folkGreen stems and leaves), and a few rocks (stone and stoneDark, faceted) with moss (moss) on top. A wooden mortar (logDark with folkRed band) with a pestle leaning in it, placed to the right of the stairs near (-1.7, z 2.5), and a fallen log and ferns near the back. All of this stays outside the stairs and the hut footprint.
parts.attaches: Disc top is groundTop (y 0.2): legs plant their feet on it and the stair ends at stairBottom (0, 0.2, 3.1). Fence gap lines up with the stairs between gatePostL and gatePostR. Rides ground.

I'm sketching the diorama's component parts: the scaly chicken legs as the base, the log-walled hut body with carved door and window frames, and a steep gabled roof with carved horse-head ridge details, shingles, and a chimney.

Next I'm sketching out the joint hierarchy, considering whether to root everything at the ground base or the hut itself.

Settling on "hut" as the root joint with spine role, I lay out the chicken-leg chains: hip, knee, ankle for each leg, then individual toe joints (three forward-facing, one hallux at back) for each foot, mirrored left and right, keeping all joint names alphanumeric without underscores. I'm also figuring out how the static base should attach—deciding it rides on the "hut" root since there's only one allowed root joint.

Working out the chicken-leg joint chain for the hut legs: hip bending forward to a knee, then back to a hock, then down to the tarsus and foot, trying to get believable bird-leg proportions and angles for each segment.

I'm also setting the bounding box for the legs part and placing the toes, spreading them forward and adding a back hallux, while checking for potential overlap between the toe spread and the front stairs geometry.

Now I'm breaking the hut body into components: chicken legs with feathered thighs, scaly shanks with spurs, and clawed toes in a yellow-and-orange folk-art palette with a budget around 190, followed by the hut walls starting with a foundation platform of root-and-bone beams beneath stacked log walls.

For the walls themselves I'm adding log ends at corner notches, chinking, a painted folk door, carved window frames with shutters, and a porch landing with railings and stairs, all at budget 200. I'm now organizing the model into five parts -- legs, hut walls with door/windows, roof and chimney, a porch with steps and lantern plus Baba Yaga's leaning mortar and pestle, and finally the diorama base with fence, skulls, and trees -- and sketching the porch's bounding box dimensions.

Working out the exact coordinates now: the hut floor platform sits around y=1.85–2.0 within its footprint, the porch landing spans z=1.3–2.0 at the same height, and I'm calculating steep stairs descending from the landing down to around z=3.3, figuring out step count and rise/run proportions to keep it feasible.

Now I'm starting to lay out the skeletal joint hierarchy for the hut structure, beginning with a root "ground" joint and a "hut" spine joint above it, defining positions and roles as I build out the rig.

Still mapping leg joint chains...

Adding scale plate bumps along the toes...

I'm deciding where the feather coverage ends along the leg, pushing the rust band down to about 80% of the way from knee to hock so it laps near the hock before transitioning to yellow tarsus coloring beyond that point.

For the feather geometry itself, since parts don't support textures, I'll build individual feather blades as extruded leaf-shaped outlines hanging downward, each defined by a local coordinate frame (sideways width, downward length) and attached to the bone, with a helper function to generate each blade's tapered leaf profile.

Now I'm tallying up my part budget of 170 total meshes — breaking down roughly how many parts each leg will need: the main leg sweep, scale details, ankle band, spur, four toes each with their own sweep/claw/knuckle components, and foot pads, to make sure I stay within the limit.

Instead of setFromUnitVectors I'll use the SDK's aim(dir, up, "y") helper to orient each feather quaternion along its direction vector. For bone assignment, thigh feathers follow hipL and knee-area feathers follow kneeL, and I'm grouping feathers by bone and color using a root-to-tip palette—rust at the root transitioning to white/black tips—possibly splitting each feather into two colored pieces to achieve that gradient.

For the layered look, I'm assigning colors by row (rust for most rows, cream and white mixed in, black-tipped near the ends) and giving each feather a small proud tip-overlay kite offset slightly along the normal for a layered feather effect, which I'll implement as a feather(pos, dir, out...) construction function.

Building the two geometries per feather and merging them into maps keyed by bone and color, then checking that the extruded mesh normals and non-indexed geometry format stay consistent across all pieces so the materials render correctly without needing extra normal recomputation.

Now I'm working out how to position feathers along the leg's thigh path: for each row and ring angle, I derive the center and tangent from the path, build a perpendicular basis using cross products with the tangent, and use that to compute the radial direction for placing each feather around the limb.

I tilt each feather outward from the tangent by about 25 degrees (increasing with shagginess), burying the root near the surface and pointing it down-out with a length of 0.32 and width of 0.17, orienting feather thickness along the radial axis. I also check that the upper feathers near the hip, around y 1.85-2.0, stay hidden under the platform since the box top sits at y=2.05.

Now I'm planning the leg's feather layout: seven rows spaced along the leg, each with about nine or ten feathers around the circumference (roughly 63-70 total per leg), with radius tapering by row using a piecewise interpolation between hip, knee, hock, and foot key radii. I'm also considering rounding off the sweep cap at the hip end.

Checking the hip sphere's geometry against the hut platform: the cap at y=1.95 with radius 0.28 would extend up to about 2.23, overlapping the platform floor at 2.0, so I'm deciding to use a flat start cap and round end cap, positioning it so the flat side sits hidden beneath the platform rather than poking visibly through.

Now I'm working out the leg's Catmull-Rom spline path starting from the hip, through a knee point, hock, and down to the ankle, adjusting coordinates so the knee bends forward and down before the leg angles back toward the hock and ankle positions.

Setting the skinning bone list to the leg chain, noting the ankle joint owns nothing past the path's end which is fine. Planning to add scale plates along the tarsus using sweep.at sampling with inherited bone weights, and sketching a sharp spur jutting off the back of the hock.

Adjusting the spur's start position to sit inside the hock joint, tagging it with the hock bone. Now I'm working out the ankle band with yellow dots, trying to figure out how to orient a ring frame along the sweep path since the sweep's normal faces outward rather than tangentially, and wrestling with how to associate the ring with the nearest bone when there's no explicit chain to reference.

I'll use a wide open-ended cylinder as the band, then add small yellow sphere dots around its ring using a local basis, merged into one part. For bone attachment, I'm reasoning that the hock joint runs from hock to ankle with the ankle at its tip, so the band should follow the hockL bone rather than ankleL.

Now I'm adding the foot pad: a yellow sphere at the ankle position, weighted to ankleL since it's the parent joint for the toes.

Writing toe sweep code...

Setting the back toe joint at y 0.3, using base-to-tip of 0.285→0.255. I'm now working out directions and lengths for each toe per leg—inner and outer toes angled slightly from center, back toe pointing backward—and tracing how the hock and tarsus connect toward the ankle.

I'm generalizing the mirroring logic so inner/outer toe directions flip sign correctly between left and right sides, using a side multiplier and consistent joint naming like toe1 through toe4 for center, inner, outer, and back toes.

Now I'm working out the claw geometry as a curved bezier shape running outward and downward from each toe tip, picking control points that bend the claw down toward the ground.

Adding claw highlight sweep...

Now I'm planning knuckle bumps on the toes—small spheres and dark scale plates placed along each toe at a couple of points for texture.

Adding ankle ball, feather tufts in rust/white/black, and a couple bone segments per leg brings each leg to around 58 parts, totaling near 116 overall, still under the 170 cap. I'll skip extra kneecap detail since feather tufts will cover that area, and just lay out plate rows along the tarsus at regular intervals.

Reworking the scale plate rows to alternate angle offsets per row for staggering, landing on about 13 plates per leg for the tarsus ring, with each plate sized as a small flattened box oriented along the surface normal and tangent flow direction.

I'm switching plate geometry to a hex cylinder shape for simplicity and rotational symmetry, with slightly smaller plates on lower rows, colored mostly scaleDark. I'm placing the ankle red band using a closest-point lookup near the tarsus end, with tarsus scale rows spanning a defined t-range and small accent dots positioned radially around the yellow spheres.

Working out band radius against the 8-sided tube's vertex geometry so a 12-sided band cylinder clears the tube's circumscribed radius, settling on roughly 1.14x the tube radius with dots placed slightly further out at the band's outer vertices.

I'm also considering adding thin yellow torus rings at the band edges as a decorative detail, then moving on to building the kite feather shape using tangent and position vectors along the path.

Writing kite geometry code...

Then I'm thinking through merging the extruded feather geometries using mergeGeometries from the BufferGeometryUtils addon, trusting the triangulation and attribute handling to work correctly.

Now I'm figuring out the feather row color pattern across the seven rows, alternating white and black tips with rust as the base, skipping an overlay on certain rows so the pattern reads naturally beneath the platform.

I'm also varying the base feather colors by row between rust shades for visual variety, and working out the draw order so lower rows of feathers overlap the upper ones properly as they fan outward and downward along the radial spacing.

Working out feather count per row based on circumference, scaling width with radius, and figuring out row spacing along the leg path from hip to knee.

Setting the color bands so the shank yellow shows between the feathers and hock, keeping the scaly-shank look readable. I'm confirming the sweep logic using bone lists and radius functions works, then setting up the aim/compose transforms so each feather orients using a quaternion toward its outward radial direction for proper thickness.

Now I'm checking that all the extruded feather geometries share compatible attribute sets for merging, and writing a basis function that computes perpendicular vectors from a tangent direction to orient each part correctly.

Working through the mirroring logic for leg paths across the s=-1/1 symmetry, and checking the hip-to-ankle point sequence for the leg curve to make sure the Catmull-Rom spline doesn't overshoot awkwardly at the knee joint.

Checking that the knee-forward, hock-backward bend matches typical chicken leg anatomy, and verifying the sweep radius is thick enough to handle the sharp joint bends without pinching at the corners.

I'll skip the ankle feather tuft and knee knuckle details to keep things simple, applying the scale plates with toe knuckle bumps on the tarsus instead. For the spur, I'm plotting a curved bezier path from the hock backward and downward to a tapered tip, giving it a tapered bone radius and a pale color.

I'll cast a ray from behind the leg into the tube surface to find the actual contact point robustly, falling back to a manual estimate if the ray misses, then anchor the spur root at that hit location for both the spur and its base sphere.

For the spur's curve, I'm plotting it to extend backward from the root, curving down and inward along four control points so it reads like a chicken's spur, then checking whether bezier accepts Vector3 inputs directly.

Writing vector helper functions...

For the ankle, I'm flattening the sphere geometry slightly with a non-uniform scale to give it a more anatomical joint shape, and setting matching radii for the tarsus and ankle transition.

Setting up imports and function signature...

Building out the leg geometry function with catmull-rom path interpolation for joint positioning...

Finishing up the color bands and checking the bone joint list, I'm noting that the ankle joint sits right at the path's end so it effectively contributes no length and gets excluded from the sweep's influence.

Now I'm generating the feather rows, computing position and tangent along the path at each row, determining radial feather counts based on circumference, and assigning bone weighting (hip vs knee) along with jittered angles and tilt per feather...

Setting up plate rows along the leg using a random generator for jitter, placing alternating angle groups per row near the hock region, then starting to define the plate stick geometry...

Thinking about whether to share the plate geometry across parts or create a fresh instance each time to avoid baking issues, then adding a decorative band of dots further up with an open-ended cylinder so only the outer faces show.

Switching to a closed cylinder for the red sleeve part since open ends made it look too flat, then placing yellow torus rings and a cluster of small spheres as decorative dots merged into the geometry.

Now I'm setting up toe configurations for each of the four toes, defining their direction, length, and radius tapers from an ankle ball joint, with three forward toes spread by offset and one shorter back toe anchored near the same base point.

Checking that the sweep angle convention keeps the claw curving upward correctly, then placing small bumps along each toe with spheres and short cylinder plates sized relative to the toe radius at that position, with the back toe getting fewer bumps than the others.

For the merge step, I'm confirming each toe bone name matches the naming scheme, skipping webbing between toes, and guarding the merge call against null geometry before combining all feather meshes per bone. Tallying up part counts per leg across the main mesh, plates, bands, rings, spurs, ankle, and toes gives roughly 51 parts per leg, so around 102 total plus the merged feather geometry.

With colors multiplied across hip and knee bones the triangle count stays manageable even with dense feather rows. I'm double-checking that unused imports like Frame get skipped while the math helpers (aim, rng, catmull, bezier) are properly exported, and that the radius function type used in the sweep is correct. Now I'm working out the claw tip path, computing control points by offsetting the tip position along the direction vector to shape the curve.

I'm planning the function that builds porch stairs using the given context object, working out the geometry for the landing and the eight descending steps.
